title: Choosing a storage service for a requirement

kcs.statement: A boot or database volume for one EC2 instance calls for EBS. Temporary, very fast scratch space that can be lost calls for instance store.
Shared file access from many Linux instances calls for EFS. Windows SMB shares or Lustre high-performance computing call for FSx.

Unlimited storage for files, backups or static web content reachable over HTTP calls for S3. Low-latency on-premises access to cloud storage calls for Storage Gateway. Centrally scheduled backups across services call for AWS Backup.

problem_ideas: Twelve one-line requirements: name the storage service and the distractor you ruled out.
A WordPress fleet behind a load balancer needs a shared uploads folder: EBS, EFS or S3, and why?
A SQL Server database on EC2 needs a fast persistent data volume: which service and volume family?
A media company serves 50 TB of videos to browsers worldwide: which storage, and which words in the stem point there?
A branch office needs SMB shares with a local cache of cloud data: which service?
Spot the trap: 'use instance store for the only copy of customer orders.'
